name: Metal woodworking tool kit in Egypt
summary: Egyptians had kits of metal-bladed tools from the later fourth millennium BC; by the Old Kingdom axes, adzes, chisels and saws were used to work wood and stone.
description: A specialist study of Egyptian copper tools reports that kits of tools with metal blades appear in the second phase of Naqada culture, in the latter half of the 4th millennium BC. The first complete collection of copper-bladed tools was found in First Dynasty Tomb 3471 at Saqqara, dated to the reign of King Djer. Old Kingdom kits most often held axes, adzes, chisels and saws, which pictures and tool marks show were used to work wood and stone in building ships and shaping statues.

impact.note: The kit served Egyptian carpenters, shipwrights and stone workers for millennia (most of one civilisation), made jointed woodwork and dressed stone possible, and a line of Egyptian woodworking and building crafts rested on it; no spread beyond Egypt is evidenced, so nothing scores 3.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Were saws among the earliest Egyptian metal kits, or do they appear only in the Old Kingdom?
A dated source for Tomb 3471 at Saqqara and the reign of Djer is needed before any year is given for the First Dynasty collection.
Whether Levantine or Balkan copper tools of the same period count as earlier, and whether Egypt's kits were independent of them.

research.note: The source records Egyptian metal-bladed kits from the late 4th millennium BC but does not say whether they were independent of earlier copper tools in the Levant or Balkans.
